The company IS funding the flat count -- shares fell 262.7m (FY2024) to 244.3m (Aug-2026). Buybacks are value-neutral here (count held flat, SBC expensed).
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 270,565,764 less treasury 26,236,282 = 244,329,482 basic at 2026-08-31 (H1 FY2027 tanshin p.2); diluted uplift from basic/diluted EPS ratio 70.62/70.53 gives ~244.6m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (0.14% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-26T05:39:53Z (intraday TSE print; replace with the regular 15:30 JST close via refresh_price)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY. Risk-free = 10y JGB ~1.8% (Oct-2026, post-BOJ normalisation); Japan ERP ~5.5% (Damodaran mature 4.6% + Japan country spread); beta ~1.0 (TOPIX retail/real-estate blend) -> cost of equity ~7.3%. Cost of debt: FY2026 non-lease finance cost ~JPY1.9bn on JPY184bn bonds/borrowings = ~1.0% pre-tax, ~0.7% after 31% tax. Weights at market: equity ~JPY690bn / debt JPY184bn (ex-lease, consistent with lease treatment B) = 79/21 -> WACC ~5.9%. Rounded UP to 6.5% for the JGB path risk (BOJ still hiking) and because the bottom-up rate is below anything this folder has used on a JPY operating company; NOT the ~9% keiretsu-supplier house reference, which encodes auto-cycle beta a prime-real-estate retailer does not carry. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, China duty-free and structural-decline risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (principal JPY26,041m in financing + interest on lease liabilities JPY4,381m, FY2026 Yuho note 'Profit or loss and cash outflow related to right-of-use assets', lines 10013-10039) = JPY30,422m = 6.8% of FY2026 revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (JPY150,069m at 2026-08-31) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: 44,290 - 20,993 = JPY23,297m = 5.2% of revenue. total_debt = bonds and borrowings only (82,209 current + 102,129 non-current).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI share of profit is tiny: -JPY203m FY2026, +87m FY2025); NCI stock JPY12,282m at 2026-08-31 is deducted ONCE in equity_bridge. No leakage driver.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (JPY WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-near-zero). ROUTING: J. Front is an operating retailer/shopping-centre operator -- Department Store 61% and SC/PARCO 28% of FY2026 segment business profit; Developer 15%; Payment & Finance 2% -- so the owner-FCF row applies, not the REIT/AFFO row (properties are PP&E/investment property at cost, no IAS 40 fair-value P&L, no external manager). A SOTP was considered and rejected as the house basis: segment capex, lease and tax splits are not disclosed, so segment cash flows cannot be built; the real-estate value is instead reported as an NAV MEMO (see valuation_philosophy) rather than put in the bridge, because the rental and property-sale income those assets generate is already inside the modelled flows (matching-asset rule). REVENUE BASIS: IFRS net 'Sales revenue' from FY2018 only; the FY2017->FY2018 drop (JGAAP gross JPY1.1tn -> IFRS net JPY470bn) is a consignment-presentation change, so no growth rate or margin crosses it. EBITDA = IFRS operating profit + D&A (FY2026 49,015 + 44,290 = 93,305, 21.0%); business profit (management's non-GAAP, 50,597) is used as the margin cross-check -- operating profit vs business profit has netted to roughly zero over FY2024-26 (gains in FY2025, Shizuoka PARCO closure loss in FY2026), so the model does not add one-offs back. last_fcf is OWNER FCF on treatment B: reported FCF (OCF 66,992 - capex 21,162 = 45,830) - SBC 616 - lease principal 26,041 = 19,173; interest income (175m) is NOT stripped because the company is net-DEBT (net debt JPY158bn), and finance income (JPY797m, mostly dividends on JPY~20bn of listed cross-shareholdings inside 'other financial assets') sits below operating profit so is outside the flows -- the matching asset is left out of the bridge too, a conservative ~JPY1-2bn omission. Note the OCF-based owner FCF (19.2bn) is LEVERED (after JPY6.0bn interest paid and JPY17.7bn cash tax, a 38% effective rate) whereas the engine builds UNLEVERED FCF at a 31% cash tax rate; FY2026 component build gives ~JPY29bn, reconciling via ~1.9bn borrowing interest, ~3.5bn tax-rate difference and ~2.6bn working-capital outflow. CAPEX: FY2026 cash capex 21,162 (PP&E 14,157 + intangibles 4,561 + investment property 2,444) = 4.75% but H1 FY2027 already 17,705 (Daimaru Umeda renovation, HAERA Nagoya, Kobe 25bankan) and the MTP committed JPY195bn over three years incl. ROU, so year-1 capex is set at 7.0% and glides to 5.0% (~= ex-ROU D&A). PRICE: TSE intraday print; after-hours not applicable.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (deducted once; flows are consolidated)

historical_growth.basis_note: IFRS basis FY2018 onward only; FY2014-FY2017 JGAAP gross sales excluded from every CAGR. 3yr = FY2023->FY2026, 5yr = FY2021->FY2026 (FY2021 is the COVID trough, so every 5yr figure is a rebound rate, not a trend). 8yr revenue FY2018->FY2026 = -0.7% is the only through-cycle revenue read.
historical_growth.eps_5yr_note: FY2021 EPS was -100.03 (COVID loss); CAGR undefined
historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = (OCF - capex) - SBC - lease principal: FY2021 9,212; FY2023 21,079; FY2026 19,173 (JPY m). Reported-FCF CAGRs would be -3.3% (3yr) and +3.9% (5yr); the gap on 5yr is because lease principal was a larger share of a smaller base in FY2021, not SBC (SBC is ~0.1% of revenue).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal JPY ~2% (Japan CPI ~2% + inbound mix) below the 3.4-5.0% equity CAGR, which was inflated by the post-COVID profit rebound and is now being deliberately shrunk by buybacks (ROE 10%+ target)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR 7.4% and EPS 3yr CAGR 27.6% diverge >30% from equity 3yr CAGR 5.0%: all three are measured off the FY2023 COVID-recovery base and overstate trend. Through-cycle IFRS revenue growth (FY2018->FY2026) is -0.7%; the base case uses 3.0% in FY2027 decaying to 1.0%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-3.1%) is below reported-FCF CAGR (-3.3%) by rounding only; SBC is immaterial in this market (JPY0.4-0.8bn/yr). The FCF decline FY2023->FY2026 despite EBITDA +37% is cash taxes (8.3bn -> 17.7bn as loss carry-forwards were used up) and capex (14.8bn -> 21.2bn).

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 guidance is sales revenue JPY470bn (+5.6%) but H1 was -2.8% and the implied H2 is +14%; haircut to +3.0% (JPY458bn) -- Umeda reopening plus HAERA plus a partial duty-free rebound, but Developer property-sale timing is the swing. Thereafter decays to Japan nominal ~1%: structural department-store decline offset by inbound and inflation.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 operating-profit EBITDA margin 21.0% (business-profit basis 21.3%); FY2027 guided business profit 53.5bn + D&A ~44bn on 470bn = 20.7%. Held 21.0% in year 1, +0.5pp over four years as Umeda/HAERA/Shibuya PARCO renovations mature and Shizuoka PARCO exits; flat thereafter.
base.capex_rationale: 7.0% in FY2027 (H1 alone JPY17.7bn; Umeda, HAERA, Kobe 25bankan) gliding to 5.0%, which is ex-ROU D&A: a 36-year-old estate cannot run below depreciation for long.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 14x FCF binds (Gordon at 6.5%/1.0% would be 18.4x). A Japanese department-store group should not be capitalised at a compounder's multiple; 14x is in line with the stock's own lease-consistent EV/EBITDA-less-lease range.

bull.narrative: FY2027 guidance met in full; SC/Developer mix shift lifts EBITDA margin to 23%; lease cost falls as Shizuoka-type exits roll off; capex normalises below D&A once the MTP projects complete; exit at 17x reflecting the real-estate backing a strategic buyer would pay for.

bear.narrative: China duty-free does not come back and domestic affluent spending rolls over with equities; FY2027 revenue flat, then the structural -1%/yr department-store decline reasserts; margin compresses to 19% on fixed costs and utilities; lease cost ratio rises on a shrinking base; renovation capex still has to be spent; zero terminal growth and a 12x exit.

scenario_narratives.base: J. Front's axes are (1) inbound/duty-free -- the late-2025 China travel advisory cut tax-free sales double digits and drove the FY2026 miss and the FY2027 operating-profit cut; (2) the affluent/gaisho domestic franchise, which is growing double digits in top-tier accounts and is the real moat; (3) the shift of profit mix toward SC (PARCO) rent and Developer fees/property sales, which is where margin can rise; (4) a 36-year-old store estate that needs continuous renovation capex (Umeda, HAERA, Kobe) against a shrinking domestic population; and (5) rising JPY rates on JPY334bn of debt-plus-leases. Base: FY2027 revenue +3% (guidance haircut for the +14% implied H2), EBITDA margin 21.0% rising to 21.5% as renovations mature, lease cost 6.8% of revenue, capex 7% falling to 5% (= ex-ROU D&A), growth decaying to 1% nominal, 6.5% JPY WACC, 14x terminal cap. Owner FCF settles around JPY30-33bn/yr.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chinese arrivals normalise and Korean/US visitors keep growing, so FY2027 hits the JPY470bn / JPY53.5bn business-profit guidance; HAERA and the Umeda relaunch prove the department-store-plus-PARCO 'fusion' model; SC and Developer carry the EBITDA margin to 23%; the next MTP (Oct-2026/Apr-2027) commits to recycling investment property (appraised JPY314bn vs JPY177bn book at FY2026) into buybacks toward the 10%+ ROE target; exit multiple 17x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Japan-China relations stay frozen, domestic wealth-effect spending fades with equities, and the structural department-store decline (-1%/yr) resumes after a flat FY2027; the Developer pipeline slips on construction costs; EBITDA margin falls to 19% on a fixed-cost estate while lease and renovation spending cannot be cut; BOJ hikes lift finance costs further (interest cover already 20x -> 11x). Owner FCF drops to ~JPY15-18bn and the business is capitalised at 12x with zero growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the company has already cut FY2027 operating-profit guidance once, the largest swing factor (Chinese tourist policy) is outside management's control, and the core format is in secular decline. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things -- duty-free recovery, MTP margin delivery, and asset recycling -- to all go right. Base 50%.

entry_price.note: House 15% hurdle applied unchanged; in JPY against a 6.5% WACC it is a very demanding bar, so the entry prices sit far below intrinsic value by construction.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis: leases charged in full (principal + interest) as an operating cost with lease liabilities excluded from net debt, cash capex restored to at least ex-ROU depreciation, cash tax at the 31% statutory rate, NCI deducted once, and a 6.5% JPY WACC built from JGB + Japan ERP. The result is deliberately a cash-flow value, not an asset value. NAV MEMO (not in the bridge): equity attributable to owners JPY416.5bn at 2026-08-31 (JPY1,703/share) plus the FY2026 investment-property appraisal surplus (fair value 314,421 - carrying 177,187 = JPY137.2bn, Yuho line 10210), net of 31% deferred tax = JPY94.7bn, gives an adjusted NAV of ~JPY511bn = ~JPY2,090/share (JPY2,265 gross of tax); the owner-occupied flagship land (Shinsaibashi, Ginza, Nagoya Sakae, Kyoto, Kobe) is in PP&E at historical cost and is NOT appraised, so true NAV is higher by an undisclosed amount. The market price is ~1.35x the disclosed adjusted NAV and ~1.66x book, and ~25x FY2026 EPS: the market is paying for real estate and a value-unlock story, not for the cash flows the stores generate. The gap between this DCF and the price is the price of that thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lease treatment: charging JPY30bn/yr of lease cash in the flows AND leaving JPY150bn of lease liabilities out of net debt is one consistent choice; treating leases as debt instead would add JPY150bn to net debt but remove ~JPY30bn/yr from the charge -- the two do not give the same answer because lease interest is low
WACC: every 50bp on a 6.5% JPY rate moves the base value ~10%; the bottom-up rate is 5.9% and the house keiretsu reference is 9%
Capex path: FY2027 run-rate (H1 JPY17.7bn) is nearly double FY2026; if MTP investment stays at 7% of revenue beyond FY2027 the base value falls further

Hidden real-estate value (investment property surplus JPY137bn, flagship land at cost) is excluded from the DCF by the matching-asset rule; an asset-recycling programme in the next MTP would realise it and is the main upside outside this model
Cash taxes: FY2026 paid JPY17.7bn (38% of PBT) vs the 31% modelled; if non-deductible closure costs recur the model is ~JPY3bn/yr generous
Revenue guidance JPY470bn needs +14% H2; base already haircuts to +3%, but Developer property-sale timing can swing FY2027 revenue by JPY10-20bn either way
